name: Travilah Oak

location.address: Potomac Oak Shopping Center, corner of Travilah Road and Glen Road, Potomac, Maryland

access: Free. Stands in the shopping centre's forecourt with a fence, patio and seating, open to anyone shopping or passing; public parking lot.
transport: About 45 to 60 minutes by car from downtown DC; Metro Red Line to Shady Grove plus a Ride On bus is the transit route (not route-checked), so a half-day trip.
verify_notes:
- Alive: Maryland Big Tree Program measured it January 2021 at 19 ft 1 in circumference (5.82 m, 582 cm), 78 ft high, 110 ft crown; enwiki says as of spring 2022 it is the Montgomery County champion white oak (a search snippet from another page says it is number two behind a tree at Wisconsin Ave and Beech Drive: conflicting, state only 'among the county's largest'). OSM node carries circumference 581 and height 23.7 m, so it was surveyed recently.
- Over 330 years old per enwiki; age is a source estimate.
- Named for postmaster Travilah Clagett. Shopping centre built 1979; threatened with removal in 1989; protection effort from 1997 (fence, patio, floodlights, lightning rods); Friends of the Travilah Oak hold an annual autumn celebration. Proposed as Maryland state tree candidate after the Wye Oak fell in 2002.
- Pin: Wikidata 39.0676,-77.2634 and OSM node 10205493991 (39.0676641,-77.263481) agree within about 8 m; OSM node is survey-grade (carries measurements).

story:
A white oak that by one estimate is older than the United States stands in the forecourt of a suburban shopping centre, behind its own fence, under its own floodlights and its own lightning rods.

Wikipedia puts the Travilah Oak at more than 330 years, a source estimate rather than a count of rings. When the Potomac Oak Shopping Center went up at the corner of Travilah Road and Glen Road in 1979, the tree was already some three centuries into its life. Ten years later it was threatened with removal. From 1997 came the protection it has today: the fence, the patio and seating around it, the lights and the lightning rods.

The Maryland Big Tree Program measured it in January 2021 at 5.82 metres round, 23.8 metres tall and with a crown 33.5 metres across. Sources disagree on whether that makes it the largest white oak in Montgomery County or the second largest, behind a tree at Wisconsin Avenue and Beech Drive.

The name comes from Travilah Clagett, a local postmaster, and the tree has a club of its own: the Friends of the Travilah Oak hold a celebration for it every autumn. When the Wye Oak, Maryland's most famous tree, fell in 2002, this one was put forward as a candidate for the state tree.

It is a long way out from the Mall, a half day by Metro and bus. It is also the rare veteran with a parking lot at its feet.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the fence, patio and floodlights around its trunk, 5.82 metres round. It stands in the forecourt of the Potomac Oak Shopping Center, at the corner of Travilah Road and Glen Road.
